name: Charles Shannon
bio: Painter and lithographer, born on 20 April 1863, the second son of a Lincolnshire country rector, and from 1881 a student at the City and Guilds Technical Art School in Lambeth, where he met Charles Ricketts (1866-1931); the two began a partnership and a shared household that lasted until Ricketts's death and never once involved living apart. Shannon was the painter of the pair and one of the first British artists after Whistler to take up lithography as an art rather than a trade, teaching himself from a printer's handbook and contributing to L'Estampe Originale in Paris; he co-founded and co-edited the Dial with Ricketts (1889-97), was art editor of the Pageant (1896-97), and became an Associate of the Royal Academy in 1911 and a full Academician in 1920. For Wilde he designed the bindings of Lady Windermere's Fan (1893), A Woman of No Importance (1894), The Importance of Being Earnest (1899) and An Ideal Husband (1899), and with Ricketts designed and decorated A House of Pomegranates (1891); Wilde nicknamed him "Marigold" and called him "the drawer of dreams", and Max Beerbohm later dubbed the two of them "the ladies of the Vale". Shannon had affairs with women, sat more than once on the edge of marrying one of his models, and did neither; his biographers divide over what to make of it, and no statement by him about his life with Ricketts in the language of sexual identity survives. In 1929 he fell while hanging a picture, suffered brain damage from which he never recovered, was nursed by Ricketts and then, after Ricketts's death, by paid nurses in Kew, and died in 1937; the collection the two men had built together passed to the Fitzwilliam Museum, Cambridge.
bio_note: Birth date (20 April 1863) and birthplace from Koenraad Claes's Y90s biography of Shannon - which gives the town as Quarrington "in the East Midlands"; "Lincolnshire" follows McKenna, The Secret Life of Oscar Wilde (2008 edn), PDF p. 190, read at the rendered page. Death year (1937) from two sources read at the rendered page: the editors' identifying footnote in Wilde's Complete Letters (2000), pp. 410-411 n. 3 ("Charles Hazlewood Shannon (1863-1937)"), and Matt Cook, Queer Domesticities (2014), printed p. 29. Conflict to resolve: Claes gives ARA 1911 and RA 1920; the Wilde editors' footnote gives "Shannon in 1921". Career detail from Claes; the household chronology, the nursing and the Kew arrangement from Cook, printed pp. 31-33 and 52; the Wilde bindings from Complete Letters p. 411 n. 3; "Marigold" and "the ladies of the Vale" from McKenna, PDF p. 190, read in the source.
